meta_title: Monny: system monitor and battery charge limit for the Mac menu bar
meta_description: A free native menu bar app for macOS: CPU, memory, disk, network, temperatures and battery in one click, history up to 7 days, and the macOS charge limit to keep a plugged-in MacBook healthy. No account, no analytics.
hero_badge: Free and open source. Nothing leaves your Mac.
hero_lead: Monny lives in the menu bar and shows CPU, memory, disk, network, temperatures and battery in one click, plus, if you like, how much of your Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Grok plan is left. It keeps a plugged-in MacBook at a healthy charge with the limit built into macOS, and costs almost nothing to run.
download_pending: The first release is coming to GitHub soon
stat_cost_label: CPU with the popover open, close to zero in the background
popover_label: The Monny menu bar popover with sample readings
battery_optimized_note: macOS learns your routine and finishes charging when you need it
features_title: Everything your Mac is doing, in one click
features_lead: Click the icon in the menu bar for the essentials. Each card opens its page in the dashboard when you want the details.
feature_cpu_text: Load on Performance and Efficiency cores, with the CPU temperature right next to it.
feature_memory_text: Used memory and memory pressure, so you see when the Mac runs short.
feature_disk_text: Free space, plus how fast the Mac reads and writes right now.
feature_network_text: Download and upload rates with a short live graph.
feature_sensors_text: CPU, GPU, SSD and battery temperatures, thermal state and fan speed.
feature_processes_text: Top apps by CPU, memory or energy, with helper processes counted under their app.
feature_menubar_text: Show CPU load, temperature or battery level right next to the icon, if you like.
feature_alerts_text: A heads-up when the Mac gets hot, memory runs short, the battery is low or one app keeps the Mac busy.
dashboard_lead: The dashboard keeps history from one minute to seven days, so you can see what slowed the Mac down an hour ago and which app was on top.
window_machine: MacBook Pro 14″ · M3 Pro · 18 GB · macOS 26
battery_title: A battery that stays healthy on the desk
battery_lead: When a MacBook lives on its charger, holding it below 100% slows battery wear. Monny sets the charge limit built into macOS 26.4 and later, right from the menu bar.
battery_point_native_text: The same charge limit as in System Settings › Battery. No helper, no administrator password.
battery_point_persist_title: Works even when Monny is closed
battery_point_persist_text: macOS keeps the limit after you quit Monny, put the Mac to sleep or restart it.
battery_point_safe_text: If the setting cannot be read on this Mac, Monny leaves it alone and says why.
battery_requirement: Charge limits need a MacBook with macOS 26.4 or later. On other Macs, monitoring works as usual. Try the slider: 100% means no limit.
ai_title: Your AI plan limits, next to CPU and memory
ai_lead: Turn on AI limits to see how much of your Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Grok plan is left and when it resets, with a heads-up when a limit is running low.
ai_note: Off by default. When it is on, Monny asks only the services you use, with the sign-in those tools already keep on this Mac.
principles_title: Built the way a Mac app should be
principle_private_text: Readings and history stay on your Mac. No account, analytics or telemetry. The only requests are update checks and the AI limits you turn on.
principle_light_text: One shared sampler reads only what is on screen, at the refresh rate you choose. About 2% CPU with the popover open and close to nothing in the background.
principle_honest_text: A sensor this Mac does not have shows as unavailable, never as a made-up zero.
principle_native_text: SwiftUI on macOS 26 with Light and Dark, keyboard, VoiceOver and six languages.
principle_free_text: MIT licensed on GitHub. No subscription and no paid tier.
principle_updates_text: Monny checks for new versions and installs them when you agree.
step1_text: Get the DMG from GitHub Releases.
step2_text: Open the DMG and drag Monny to the Applications folder.
step3_text: Monny appears in the menu bar and walks you through three short steps.

install_command_label: Terminal command that allows Monny to open
faq_free_a: Yes. Monny is free and open source under the MIT license, with no subscription, account or paid features.
faq_mac_a: Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 26 or later. Intel Macs are not supported. The charge limit also needs a MacBook with macOS 26.4 or later.
faq_limit_q: How does the charge limit work?
faq_limit_a: Monny changes the charge limit built into macOS, the same one as in System Settings › Battery, and macOS enforces it. It stays on after Monny quits, during sleep and after a restart. macOS may charge a few percent above the limit and occasionally to 100% to keep its battery estimate accurate.
faq_cost_q: Will Monny slow my Mac down?
faq_cost_a: No. One shared sampler reads only what is on screen, at the refresh rate you choose. With the popover open it uses about 2% CPU, and close to nothing in the background.
faq_privacy_q: Does Monny send my data anywhere?
faq_privacy_a: No. Readings and history stay on your Mac. Monny goes online only to check for updates and, if you turn on AI limits, to read those limits from the services you use.
faq_warning_q: Why does macOS say it cannot verify Monny?
faq_warning_a: Monny is signed, but Apple notarization needs a paid Developer ID that the project does not have yet. Allow it once in System Settings › Privacy & Security, or with the Terminal command in the install section.
faq_sensors_a: Sensors differ between Mac models. When a Mac does not report a temperature, fan or battery reading, Monny says it is unavailable instead of showing a made-up value.
cta_title: Take a calm look at your Mac
cta_text: Free for macOS 26 and later on Apple silicon.
not_found_text: Like a sensor this Mac does not have: Monny would rather say so than make up a reading. The page you are looking for is not here.
